function: Predicts top-M beams from a 64-beam codebook for 60 GHz V2I and V2V links, using GPS position, camera images and LiDAR point clouds (p. 5, 9).
system: Phased-array unit (BS/RSU or vehicle) with 16-element ULA and 64-beam codebook, single-antenna transmitting vehicle; 60 GHz, OFDM; V2I and V2V; no RIS (p. 5, 9-10).
method: Multimodal CNN: 1D-CNN for position, fine-tuned EfficientNet-B0 for images, fine-tuned PointNet for LiDAR; concatenation and two dense layers; supervised, cross-entropy, Adam (p. 6-9).
data_channel: DeepSense 6G measured data: V2I scenarios 31-34 and V2V scenarios 36-39 (60 GHz, 64 beams), GPS, camera, LiDAR; each scenario split 60/20/20 (p. 9-10).
test_conditions: Trained and tested within each scenario on a 60/20/20 split (train/validation/test); averaged over 5 runs; no cross-scenario test; suggests continual updating for new settings (p. 10).
baselines: 5G-NR exhaustive beam sweep over all 64 beams (non-learned) compared on sweeping time and search space; no learned baseline or other method compared (p. 12).
metrics: Top-M accuracy (M=1, 5, 9, 13), received power ratio, beam sweeping time and search-space overhead, inference time 0.5-1.0 ms (p. 10-13).
complexity: Average inference time per sample 0.5-1.0 ms on RTX 2080 GPU; no parameter or FLOP count (p. 12).
openness: Code on GitHub: github.com/mbaqer/V2X-mmWave-Beamforming; public DeepSense 6G dataset (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 9: "DeepSense 6G dataset [65], [66], a collection of real-world mmWave sensing and communications measurements"; the model is trained and tested on this measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "train the model on splitted training samples of each individual scenarios"; testing uses the held-out 20% of the same scenario (60/20/20 split); no cross-scenario, new-site or fine-tuning test is reported, only a suggestion to keep updating the model (p. 10).
q3_support: p. 12: "we compare the performances of our proposed approach against standard defined existing beam selection approach in terms of beam sweeping latency and beam searching space overheads"; only the non-learned 5G-NR exhaustive search is compared, and no earlier learned method appears in the results (Table II, p. 4, only surveys related works).
q4_support: p. 12: "the average inference execution time (per sample) measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 GPU is roughly between 0.5 ms and 1.0 ms"; a measured runtime of the proposed model; no parameter or FLOP count is given.
q5_support: p. 10: "implementation codes along with detailed instructions are publicly available"; footnote 3 gives https://github.com/mbaqer/V2X-mmWave-Beamforming; the data are the public DeepSense 6G scenarios (p. 9).
notes: Beam prediction for the phased-array unit is area 3 (beams); the array has 16 elements, so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply. The DOI printed on p. 1 matches (arXiv 2504.06173v1, accepted version). Top-13 accuracy is 98.19% for V2I and 66.96% for V2V (p. 10). q4 rests on the measured inference time, not on the beam sweeping time, which is signaling overhead.
